ops.body:
- **T? [owner] Walkability: ground nobody read looks the same as plain ground** (2026-11-27)
  Area: walkability. Seen: since G5 (specs/walkability-car-ground) ground easy on foot is the plain map, so plain also means "neither" and "not read": past the 1.5 km read, or where a tile could not be read, the map looks like ground easy on foot (the review pictures, `g5/review2/after-fade-132-390.png`). Rests on: the owner, in person, 2026-11-27, asked by the steward ("With foot ground drawn as the plain map, plain now also means 'not read' and 'neither'. Is that acceptable, or should unread ground ever look different?"): "Unread should differ".
  Recommended: a thin dashed line in the map's neutral grey along the edge of what was read, drawn only while the layer is on and the edge is in view, and the layer's note one clause longer: "the dashed line is as far as it has read". No fill, no number; the hatch keeps its fade inside the line. /vision: aligned (earn: says what the map knows; Always, "Restraint in motion, colour and copy").
  Precedent: none found for a walkability layer; weather radar apps (RainViewer, MyRadar) draw the edge of coverage as a line and leave the rest plain (from memory, unverified; not yet recorded).
  Otherwise: a faint neutral veil over unread ground (heavier: grey already means "not loaded"), or leave it.

- **T? [owner] Walkability: a screen wholly inside car ground has no edge to say what the hatch is** (2026-11-27)
  Area: walkability. Seen: the steward's review of G5's built screens (2026-11-27): "When the walker stands inside a large car area, the whole screen is hatch with no edge in view: does the hatch alone still say 'built around cars', or is that where the quiet label (G5's 'After it') is owed?"; the ux-reviewer's cold find got "car" from the heads-up's words, not the map. Rests on: G5's "After it" ("a quiet label inside large car areas, if the hatch alone does not say it"); `docs/research/walkability-car-ground.md`, option D.
  Recommended: one quiet label, "Built around cars", in slate at the map's own label size, inside each car area larger than the screen at walking zoom, placed by the map like a street's name (one per area, none on a small area, never a number). /vision: aligned if quiet (earn; Always, "Restraint"; Never, tallies: no count).
  Precedent: aviation charts name restricted airspace inside its hatched boundary (search summary, unverified; docs/research/adjacent-apps.md, "Mark ground that is hard on foot").
  Otherwise: leave it to the heads-up and the legend.

- **T? [owner] Walkability: the legend no longer says what plain ground means** (2026-11-27)
  Area: walkability. Seen: since G5 the legend has one row, "Built around cars" (`src/lib/layers/registry.ts`); "Easy on foot" left with its tint. The steward (2026-11-27): "With 'Easy on foot' gone from the legend, plain ground is not explained anywhere: should the note say so until 'Unread should differ' is built?" Rests on: Nielsen Norman Group heuristic 6, recognition rather than recall (docs/research/ui-references.md).
  Recommended: the layer's note gains one sentence, "Ground left plain is easy on foot or mixed." (words only; no new row, no number); with the unread line built (its own entry), "or not read yet" joins it. /vision: aligned (earn; words that describe, never judge).
  Precedent: none found (a legend that explains its absence of fill; not yet recorded).
  Otherwise: leave the note as it is until the unread ground differs.

ops.body: - [loop] The car ground's fade ends at a third of the hatch's strength at the edge of what was read, so zoomed out it still reads as an edge (specs/walkability-car-ground, the owner's look check of 2026-11-27, "Publish as is", told so; polish, low). Not built: a third step toward nothing, or the last step thinned, shown to the owner first.

argv: The car ground's fade ends at a third
ops.body: - [loop] The legend's hatch swatch reads faint, and its cased route sample reads as a plain blue line at legend size (specs/walkability-car-ground, the owner's look check of 2026-11-27, "Publish as is", told so; polish, low). Not built: a stronger swatch line or a wider slate casing in the sample, shown to the owner first.

- [loop] chronicles-data's fetches report every non-answer as 'timed out': `src/http.ts` (l.38 swallows a rejected fetch, l.53 throws SourceTimeout for a null response, a 500 or a 504), so the owner's manual build of Nov 26 (run 45912355660) could not tell a server error from a dropped connection when us-northeast failed twice in under a second at 23:56Z (no timer fired; Geofabrik's nightly renewal was near) (found by the session's diagnosis run, Nov 27, low; no code bug in T66). Fix: name the status or the fetch error's cause in the message, keeping SourceTimeout for what the Wikidata adapter splits a cell on.

- [loop] chronicles-data's OSM fetch gives up after two tries 30 s apart (`TRIES = 2`, the source's pace), so one bad half-minute costs the whole week's OSM answers (Nov 26: both tries failed; run 40 of Nov 23 had three such non-answers, each healed by its retry) (found Nov 27, low). Optional: a third try after a longer wait for a non-answer.

**Nov 27, `/tend inbox G5 yes`: walkability, only the car ground, hatched, and its stretch on the route** (opened from `d6a69cae`; G5, "Walkability: only the car ground, hatched, and its stretch on the route", the owner's yes of Nov 22, "Yes, queue it (Recommended)"; built as `specs/walkability-car-ground`, CG1-CG11, decisions 0232, 0271; an inbox run, so lenses 1-7 were not run).
- The look, the owner's in person, Nov 27, on the web build: "A (Recommended)" from four candidates, then "Too 'keep out'", then "Soft A2 (Recommended)" (45°, 9 px apart, 1.25 px at 40%); "Fade over ~100 m (Recommended)"; "Everywhere (Recommended)" (the car icon slate on the heads-up and the legend); after the diff review "Mark where it starts (Recommended)", "Edge to 3:1, lines soft (Recommended)", "Square swatch, no box border", "Add a cased route sample", "Hold at every zoom (Recommended)"; on the look check "Publish as is".
- Built: only the ground built around cars is drawn, a slate hatch held near 9 px apart at every zoom (four images a quarter zoom apart), its 1 px edge at 3:1, the cells joined and rounded on a 25 m lattice, fading in two 50 m steps toward the edge of what was read; the route's stretch through it cased in slate, cut from the drawing, with a slate dot where it starts; the legend's one row with the hatch and a cased route; the web and native maps (native unverified).
- The cells' rule and the area card's words unchanged: an old/new differential over the five real fixtures, 482 cells and 15 card lines, no difference.
- Reviews: the steward on the plan, 5 accepted and 3 the owner's (walkability-car-ground audit 1-4); the diff, one round, the steward, the ux-reviewer and the auditor, every finding accepted as ruled (audit 5-16; the auditor's F1 high, the fade, rebuilt), 0 rejected.
